artifacts.summary: Seven-phase sequential plan for the universal cover of a doubly serial digraph: a ForMathlib rank/parent acyclicity criterion, a Saturation-parameterised FrameOver constructor, the reduced-walk carrier, the oriented-forest fields, the one-step and iterated lifts, two-way boundedness, and the L-plus truth-transfer assembly.

memory_candidates.content: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh assembles a plan's '## Lean Challenge Statements' section by concatenating every ```lean fenced block, then rewriting each recognized declaration from its top-level ':=' onward to ':= sorry'. Two consequences constrain how the section must be authored. (1) Everything between one declaration's ':=' and the next declaration's start is DISCARDED, so any import, namespace, open or end line sitting between two declarations vanishes: the section must be ONE fenced block whose entire preamble (all imports and all open lines) precedes the first declaration, with no namespace blocks between declarations. (2) Declaration names are harvested as a single dot-free identifier, so 'def FrameOver.ofStepSat' harvests as 'FrameOver' and fails the hard cross-validation against the Goals identifier set; declare at the root and name the real namespace in prose instead. Verify both at plan time with '--dry-run' (fast, prints the assembled module and the harvested theorem_names) and then '--dry-run --compile' (compiles in a scratch dir against the project's own toolchain), which catches an unstatable pinned signature before any implementation dispatch runs.
